purpose: Defines the six-phase workflow for creating visual design (design tokens, component visual specs, UX evaluation) from a requirements document, driven by a confirmed Design Intent.
summary: Positioning in the pipeline: input is a requirements document, output is THEME, CMP and UXEVAL documents
Context management: per-phase knowledge retrieval via query-forge-rules, with design_philosophy always resident
Phase 1: load requirements, collect reference designs, fetch rule documents
Phase 2.0: acquire and confirm Design Intent (tension axis, distinctiveness importance, references, anti-goals, signature requirement)
Phase 2: design direction (personality, tension axis, reference cultures, provocations, recommendation, confirmation) with conditional activation
Phase 3: design tokens (colors, light/dark, typography, spacing, radius/shadow, signature tokenization, quality checklist)
Phase 4: convert ASCII screen layouts to component visual specs, naming, states, UX notes, signature placement
Phase 5: UX self-evaluation (Norman, Rams, HIG/Nielsen/Gestalt, distinctiveness/memorability metrics)
Phase 6: generate documents, AI review, specs ToC update, commit confirmation, completion guidance
Dialogue principles and anti-patterns such as ungrounded design and platform confusion
tasks: Creating visual design from a requirements document
Designing design tokens (colors, typography, spacing, radius)
Defining or confirming a Design Intent
Evaluating UX quality and distinctiveness of a design
title: UX/UI デザイン創造ワークフロー
